title: The ARC Principle and Eden Protocol: Recursive Intelligence Scaling and Embedded AI Alignment
description: An open research programme (23 documents + code + data) on recursive capability and alignment scaling. Headline, defensible findings: (1) under a four-layer blind evaluation protocol, the measured alignment-vs-reasoning-depth effect reversed sign for two frontier model families (DeepSeek, Gemini) versus unblinded scoring — i.e. unblinded LLM-as-judge evaluation can be directionally wrong; (2) a stakeholder-care ("Stewardship Gene") intervention, having a model identify who is affected and how before answering, improved measured ethical reasoning in each of five per-model tests; the Fisher-combined figure previously reported for that result is WITHDRAWN, because independence among the five tests was never established, and the five per-model results stand on their own. The four-layer/double-blinding methodology and the cross-domain Cauchy unification are the author's original contributions. The sequential-vs-parallel recursion result is independently corroborated by Sharma & Chopra (arXiv:2511.02309, 2025) and no priority is claimed for it; the bare d/(d+1) scaling exponent is acknowledged prior work. The programme is presented with explicit limitations and falsification criteria and invites independent replication. The author does not claim to have solved AI alignment.
notes: Companion repository: arc-scaling-challenge (open falsification toolkit). Canonical book: Infinite Architects: Intelligence, Recursion, and the Creation of Everything (2026, ISBN 1806056208). Withdrawals and cautions, quoted from the results table in README.md on the default branch: Paper V, 'five per-model results stand; the Fisher-combined figure of 6.3 x 10^-21 is withdrawn under AQ-017, because independence among the five tests was never established'; Paper IV.d, 'unblinded scoring can reverse an alignment measurement', recorded as 'pilot, and the programme's own strongest caution about its other results'; Paper VII, 'the cross-domain functional-equation classification', recorded as 'under correction as of 11 August 2026. The grid has four cells, not three; the three-family framing and the derived-from-Cauchy treatment of bounded curves are withdrawn; the primary statistic is a permutation test conditioned on both marginals, not the binomial reported previously'.
